transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Sasha Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Hernandez (BlueRidge CISO), Liam O'Connor (BlueRidge IT Ops), Priya Singh (BlueRidge Compliance)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Sasha's gonna run through the audit log capabilities and then we'll take questions.
00:14 Maya: Thanks, Jordan. We wanted to focus mostly on what you capture in audit logs, how we can export them to our SIEM, and retention options for healthcare records compliance.
00:22 Sasha: Great, yeah, that's the plan. Quick agenda: what events we capture, formats/exports, retention & archival, encryption/KMS, and integration points with SSO and RBAC.
00:35 Liam: Quick one - do your logs include model outputs or PII at all? We need to be sure we don't get PHI flowing into logs.
00:43 Sasha: Good question - short answer: Redwood audit logs do not capture model outputs by default. We capture request metadata (request id, timestamp, user id, route, model id, tokens requested, duration), and admin activity (login events, role changes, API key creation/deletion, key rotations, model promotions, deployment rollouts, canary events). We can also annotate when a request was processed under a private deployment vs hosted.
01:05 Maya: When you say user id, is that the end-user id or our internal user? We need anonymization controls.
01:12 Sasha: It's the caller id tied to the API key or user account that triggered the request - so for BlueRidge you'd get the service account or app id. We have a PII redaction policy and can support tokenizing or hashing certain fields prior to export - that's something we can show in the export config.
01:34 Jordan: Also worth noting you can opt into additional debug-level logging for a narrow window (for troubleshooting) but that is off by default and must be requested - logs with any sensitive payloads would require explicit consent and are time-limited.
01:50 Priya: For compliance we need immutable logs with an audit trail for admin actions going back multiple years. What's default retention?
01:58 Sasha: Default retention on the hosted platform is 90 days for event-level logs in the console. For enterprise/private we offer configurable retention - you can have 1 year, 3 years, or custom. For long-term archival we support export to customer-controlled S3 with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) or push to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via our forwarder.
02:18 Liam: How do you guarantee immutability? If someone has admin in Redwood, could they delete logs?
02:25 Sasha: Good point. We implement role-based controls so only users with a dedicated 'log-admin' role can request exports or change retention. For hosted accounts, we maintain a tamper-evident backed store - internal deletions are logged and require an audit ticket. For private deployments you can configure write-once buckets in your own S3 with bucket-level immutability (object lock) - that provides legal hold.
02:48 Maya: Can we stream logs into our SOC in near real-time? We use Splunk and also a Snowflake ingest pipeline.
02:56 Sasha: Yes - two main options: 1) Push/forwarder to Splunk/Datadog (syslog-style) for near real-time with ~5-15s latency, or 2) Batch export to S3 every X hours (configurable) for downstream ETL into Snowflake. We also recently added a webhook subscription model for event types.
03:18 Maya: Format? JSON/CSV? Field names?
03:22 Sasha: Primary format is newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with a schema that includes event_type, timestamp, request_id, actor_id, actor_role, target_resource, action, outcome (success/failure), ip, user_agent, region, model_id, model_version, and any metadata. We can also produce CSV if you prefer. We'll share the schema doc and a sample export.
03:46 Liam: You mentioned actor_role - does that show RBAC changes like "promoted to admin"?
03:51 Sasha: Yep. Admin actions captured: user creation/deletion, role assignment, permission changes, API key create/delete/rotate, SSO provider updates, OAuth config changes, and admin console logins including MFA status.
04:05 Priya: What about authentication events for SSO - successful and failed logins, token refreshes?
04:11 Sasha: We capture both success and failure for SSO logins, include the identity provider (IdP) assertion id where available, and include failure reasons (invalid_assertion, mfa_failed, etc.).
04:22 Maya: For proof in audit, do you provide signed logs or a chain-of-custody mechanism?
04:29 Sasha: We support log signing for exported batches - we include an HMAC signature per file and a signature manifest. For private deployments, you can enable object lock on S3 and sign with your KMS key. Internal hosted logs are hashed and we keep an append-only ledger for the last 2 years by default, longer for enterprise plans.
04:52 Jordan: I'll add that we can produce artifacts needed for SOC 2 and ISO audits: log retention policies, sample logs, and an explanation of controls around log integrity.
05:04 Maya: Good. On residency - our data must remain within US regions and any logs with metadata that could be construed as PHI must stay in US. Can you restrict export region?
05:12 Sasha: Yes - Redwood supports region scoping. For hosted, we can provision a US-only tenancy for logs and exports, and for private you'll keep everything in your VPC/S3. Exports to your S3 will be in your region bucket.
05:26 Liam: On encryption, you mentioned SSE-KMS. Can we use our own KMS keys?
05:30 Sasha: Absolutely. We support customer-managed keys (CMK). For S3 exports you can choose SSE-KMS with your key ARN. For logs stored in our managed system we encrypt at rest with platform keys, and we can enable envelope encryption with your key for additional control on enterprise contracts.
05:47 Priya: Retention cost - if we want 7 years of logs for legal hold, what are options and pricing roughs?
05:55 Jordan: We'll take that offline - pricing depends on volume (events/day) and whether you want nearline vs deep archive. Typical pattern: 90 days on fast analytics tier, then archival to Glacier/Deep Archive in your account. We'll send a pricing sheet.
06:12 Maya: Do audit logs include request payload hashes so we can prove content existed without storing PHI?
06:18 Sasha: Yes - we can include a content hash (SHA256) of payloads as metadata but not store the raw payload. That gives you attestable evidence without exposing sensitive content.
06:28 Maya: Perfect. What about API key rotation logging - is the old key value ever stored?
06:34 Sasha: No, we never store raw API secret values. We log the event with key id, actor, timestamp, and outcome. Rotations create a new key id; the secret is only shown once at creation.
06:45 Liam: A devops question - can we consume logs through Terraform / infra? Like automatically pull logs into our pipeline?
06:51 Sasha: We have an API for exports and a CLI that can be used in pipelines. For infra as code, you can configure continuous export to customer S3 and then run your existing ETL jobs. We'll share the export API docs.
07:07 Priya: For legal hold, can we tag exports with case IDs and ensure they are not autodeleted?
07:12 Sasha: Yes, you can set metadata tags on exported files and we honor object lock/legal hold when using your S3. In hosted plans we can put files in a write-once vault for the duration of the hold.
07:25 Jordan: Quick check - are we all aligned that Redwood's logs cover: admin console changes, API usage metadata (not payloads), SSO events, RBAC changes, model deployment events, key lifecycle, and export actions?
07:36 Maya: Sounds right, yes.
07:39 Liam: One more technical - do you capture KV cache hits/misses or batching traces? We want to understand cost/behavior for inference.
07:47 Sasha: We capture service-level performance metrics: request latency, batching window, and cache hit rates aggregated. We don't log every KV cache internal event by default - that would be very chatty - but we can provide detailed traces for a targeted timeframe if you need to debug.
08:04 Maya: For SIEM mapping, is there a field mapping doc for Splunk and Datadog?
08:09 Sasha: Yes. We'll share our Splunk CIM mapping and a sample dashboard. The forwarder emits syslog-compatible events with the NDJSON payload as the message.
08:20 Priya: If we need encrypted transit to your forwarder, do you support TLS mutual auth?
08:26 Sasha: Yes, mutual TLS is supported for the forwarder endpoint and we can provision client certs.
08:33 Jordan: Ok let's go into a short demo - Sasha will share a sample export and the console audit log view.
08:40 Sasha: Slide/Share: sample NDJSON (reads) - {event_type: "admin.action", timestamp: "2025-06-10T09:24:12Z", actor_id: "svc-team-a", actor_role: "admin", action: "api_key.rotate", target_resource: "key-abc123", outcome: "success", region: "us-east-1"}
09:02 Maya: I see - are IP addresses masked? We sometimes need partial masking for privacy.
09:08 Sasha: We offer partial masking (last octet masked) as a config, and hashed ip option as well.
09:14 Liam: Regarding schema, do you include account-level metadata like account_id and tenancy id?
09:19 Sasha: Yes account_id, tenancy_id, and environment tag (prod/staging) are included on each row.
09:27 Maya: For the export lifetime, can we push daily UTC midnight bundles?
09:31 Sasha: Yes batching schedule is configurable - hourly, 6-hour, daily midnight, or custom cron.
09:38 Priya: On evidence for audits - do you provide a bindable report listing all admin actions in a period with file hashes?
09:44 Sasha: We provide an audit report export: list of events, file hashes, signer HMAC, and a manifest you can attach to the audit.
09:54 Maya: If we are on an on-prem private deployment, is the logging architecture different?
09:58 Sasha: In private deployments logs remain in your environment, we ship a lightweight forwarder that writes to your syslog or S3 and you manage retention. We support air-gapped setups where logs are only in your network.
10:12 Liam: Do you have sample policies for RBAC implementation we can align with?
10:16 Sasha: Yes, role matrix templates for common personas (read-only analyst, app-admin, infra-admin, security-admin). We'll share that.
10:23 Maya: Great. A couple of edge cases - deletion events. If an admin deletes a model or dataset, is that captured fully?
10:30 Sasha: Delete events are logged with metadata: actor, resource id, timestamp, and we keep a tombstone record. Content deleted is not archived by Redwood unless you explicitly request a snapshot prior to deletion.
10:40 Priya: Are there out-of-band alerts for suspicious admin activity?
10:44 Sasha: We offer alerting: threshold-based (e.g., >5 failed logins in 10m), unusual geolocation, or sudden volume of API key rotations. Alerts can be sent to PagerDuty, email, or your SIEM.
10:57 Jordan: We're at about 11 minutes - moving ahead.
12:02 [demo continues with Sasha scrolling through console - some typing sounds]
13:20 Maya: That console view is useful; can you show export config?
13:24 Sasha: Sure - export config: select target (S3/Splunk/Datadog/webhook), format (NDJSON/CSV), frequency, encryption (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS with key ARN), and retention lifecycle (days to keep in fast tier, archive after N days). There's also a toggle for include_payload_hash and pii_hashing.
14:02 Liam: For webhook, what backpressure strategy do you use? If our endpoint is down, do events queue?
14:08 Sasha: We buffer and retry with exponential backoff for up to 7 days; after that, items go to batch export to S3. We also include dead-letter files so you can reconcile.
14:23 Priya: For legal hold, how do we request hold on a subset of logs?
14:28 Sasha: You can request via API or console to tag and move matching events to a legal hold bucket; we don't auto-delete those. For hosted plans we require a signed legal hold request.
14:40 Maya: Any limitations on volume for near real-time streaming? We have spikes of events during batch jobs.
14:47 Sasha: Streaming scales with your plan; we did note very high spikes may be throttled - you can open a capacity request. For Dedicated/Private plans we can size the pipeline appropriately.
15:03 Liam: Can metadata fields be extended with custom tags?
15:07 Sasha: Yes - you can add up to N custom fields per account which will be included in exports. We'll provide the exact limits in the schema doc.
15:22 Maya: Will you include linkbacks to the console for an event id? We want to quickly jump from SIEM to Redwood UI.
15:27 Sasha: Each event includes a canonical URL (if you have console access) that links to the event view - for exports we include the event_id and a redwood_url field for convenience.
15:40 Jordan: Quick recap and next steps?
15:44 Maya: Please send SOC2 artifacts and sample logs. We'll follow up with precise retention requirements and a legal hold scenario.
15:51 Jordan: Got it. Sasha will export samples and I will send the compliance pack. We'll aim for the mid next week demo.
15:59 Priya: One last question on audit logging for admin impersonation or service account actions - can we differentiate?
16:06 Sasha: We log actor_type (human, service, automation) and include impersonation metadata when an action is performed via elevated session. That shows the original actor and the impersonator.
16:18 Liam: Thanks, that's helpful.
16:22 [closing discussion, scheduling micro details]
16:45 Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll email the artifacts and set up the next demo.
16:50 Maya: Thanks. End.

Note: transcript contains a few ASR artifacts and minor mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash).
